subject: Throughput drop observed: coordinated customer updates & mitigation
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: [ALERT] Significant throughput drop across us-west model pool

Marissa —

We started seeing a sustained throughput drop (~40% throughput relative to baseline) in the us-west serving pool beginning ~09:55 PT. Latency (p95) has climbed from ~120ms to ~980ms for customer traffic hitting the gpt-vert model group. Error rate is still low, but the queue depth is growing and autoscaler isn’t returning to target.

Immediate observations:
- Rolling back to the previous kernel variant temporarily restores throughput for small batches (10-15% improvement) but doesn’t hold for longer sequences.
- KV cache hit rate is ~12% lower than expected (possible cache eviction/segmentation issue).
- No obvious infra node failures in metrics; CPU on the inference controller spiked at 100% around 09:58.

I’m attaching logs and a p95 chart snapshot. I’ve opened PD-48291 and flagged this as high-priority.

This looks like it will affect a few mid-sized customers; Finova is already seeing degraded throughput and pinged CS. Priority: we need a short internal playbook + a customer-friendly update in the next 90 minutes.

Immediate asks:
- Dev: can you confirm whether the kernel fallback is safe for traffic right now and whether we can apply it globally (risk of regressions)?

I’ll draft a short version for Finova and post in the incident Confluence page for approvals. If we need to offer credits or a temporary routing change (dedicated pool), flag it here.

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Significant throughput drop across us-west model pool

Quick update after a short investigation:

Root-cause hypothesis:
- A recently deployed kernel selector change (rolled 03/04) has an incorrect eviction heuristic under mixed short/long sequence traffic. That is causing excessive KV cache churn which forces more compute for context reloading.

Safe mitigations we can do now:
- Roll back kernel selector (fast, low-risk): restores ~20-30% throughput for most workloads. Will run in the next 15m if SRE gives the go-ahead.
- Force route Finova (and other affected customers) to the dedicated pool in us-east while we stabilize (requires ops change and customer consent).
- Increase autoscaler headroom temporarily + tune controller CPU limit to avoid the spike.

Risks:
- Global rollback may mask underlying bug; we should keep a canary with the new selector for telemetry.
- Routing to dedicated pool may increase their cost. Sales/CS should approve.

I can prepare the rollback and a short runbook. ETA for a measurable improvement after rollback: ~10–12 minutes. Full stabilization depends on cache warm-up (~30–45 minutes).

—Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Wu <tom.wu@finova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>, Support Team <support@finova.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: [Proposed] Brief update on degraded performance — Finova

Tom —

We’re seeing a performance degradation that may affect request throughput to some models in the us-west region; our engineers are actively working on it. We wanted to share a short status update and next steps: 

Current status (12:05 PT):
- Impact: intermittent increased latencies and reduced throughput for a subset of requests.
- Scope: Finova traffic routed to the us-west pool may see 2x p95 latency briefly; error rates remain within acceptable bounds.
- What we’re doing: engineering is rolling back a recent runtime selector change and applying temporary autoscaler headroom adjustments.

Customer-facing ETA:
- Short-term improvement expected within ~15 minutes after the rollback.
- Full stabilization (cache warm-up) within 30–45 minutes.

If you prefer, we can temporarily route Finova traffic to a dedicated pool in us-east while we complete stabilization; that would require brief coordination and may impact costs. Please let us know if you want us to initiate that.

We’ll send a follow-up once we have confirmation the rollback succeeded.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
